pages.text:
“Hey, Dudu,” Dumisani says.
“I bet you can’t throw
your hat through
that window.”
pages.action: Dumisani dares Dudu to throw her hat through the window
pages.change: A dare sets the goal of the story
pages.question_created: Can Dudu get her hat through the window?
pages.page_turn_note: The dare is open; the turn shows her looking at the target.

notes: Dumisani whispers behind his hand with a wide grin; Dudu answers with a narrowed, sceptical look
A stuffed rhino sits on the shelf under the window
illustration.only_in_image: The stuffed rhino is planted on the shelf here, three spreads before a hat lands on its head; Dumisani's cupped hand shows the dare is a conspiratorial secret.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Dudu looks up at the open window.
It’s so high up the classroom wall,
she can’t see what’s on the other side.
pages.action: Dudu looks up at the window, too high to see through
pages.change: The target is shown to be high and unknown
pages.question_created: What is on the other side of the window?
pages.page_turn_note: The story never answers what is outside; the window stays a blank sky.

notes: Small figures under a tall wall make the window look far away
Dumisani points up eagerly; Dudu looks worried
illustration.only_in_image: Scale carries the difficulty: two small children far below the window. Dudu's worry and Dumisani's eagerness are shown, not said.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“OK,” says Dudu.
“I’ll count to three.”
They take their hats off
and stand ready.
“One…” says Dudu slowly,
“two”…
“THREE!”
pages.action: Dudu counts to three, slower then louder
pages.change: They take their hats off and get ready
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends on the shouted third number; the throw itself is on the next spread.

notes: The count is set in growing type, the last number largest
Dumisani grins and wiggles his fingers; Dudu looks nervous, mouth round
illustration.only_in_image: Rising type size makes the countdown loud for the reader-aloud; Dudu's nervousness is only in her face.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Dudu and Dumisani throw their hats
towards the window.
Dudu’s hat lands softly against the
wall and slides down onto the shelf
underneath.
But Dumisani’s hat gets close.
It hits the windowsill and rebounds,
turning three times in the air before
coming to rest on the head of
the stuffed rhino below.
pages.action: Both hats miss; Dumisani's bounces and lands on the rhino's head
pages.change: The first try fails in a funny way

notes: Red motion lines trace both throws from off the left page to the wall and the rhino
Wobble lines around the rhino as the hat lands
illustration.only_in_image: The drawn trajectories show exactly how each hat travels and where it stops, which the text only lists; the rhino looks startled.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Dudu and Dumisani laugh so hard,
Dudu has to hold her tummy.
“Again!”
she says.
pages.action: They laugh hard; Dudu asks to go again
pages.change: Failure turns into a game they want to repeat
pages.question_created: Will it work the next time?

notes: Dumisani hugs the rhino still wearing his hat
Both laugh with eyes shut, radiating lines
illustration.only_in_image: Dumisani holding up the hatted rhino is the joke they are laughing at; the text only says they laugh.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
The friends fetch their hats,
and Dumisani counts,
“One, two, three!”
Dumisani’s hat sails through the air,
makes it past the windowsill,
bumps against the frame
and falls through the window.
“YES!” he shouts.
Dudu’s hat is on
the shelf again.
pages.action: Dumisani counts; his hat goes through; Dudu's lands on the shelf again
pages.change: Dumisani succeeds and Dudu is left behind

notes: Dumisani punches the air; Dudu looks down at her hat with a sad, sideways frown
Hat drawn just passing the window frame
illustration.only_in_image: Dudu's disappointment is only in the picture: the text reports where her hat is, not how she feels.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Do it again,”
Dumisani says to Dudu.
Dudu gets her hat, balls it up in her hand
and squints at the window.
“One, two, three,”
says Dumisani, and Dudu throws.
But her hat bounces off the windowsill
and slides down the wall again.
“Again”
says Dumisani.
pages.action: Dudu balls up her hat and throws again; it bounces off the sill
pages.change: A second failure; Dumisani urges again

notes: Dudu grits her teeth with an angry squiggle over her head
Dumisani cheers with arms wide while her hat drops past the rhino
illustration.only_in_image: Dudu's rising anger (gritted teeth, squiggle) and Dumisani's unthinking cheerfulness are only in the picture; the balled-up hat that will matter later is drawn in flight.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Uh uh,” says Dudu.
“Let’s go outside
to the swings.”
She fetches her hat
and puts it firmly
on her head.
“Ah, please, Dudu?”
says Dumisani.
“Here, I’ll help you.”
pages.action: Dudu refuses, jams her hat on and wants the swings; Dumisani pleads and offers help
pages.change: Dudu gives up; Dumisani switches from daring to helping
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends on an offer of help; the help itself is on the next spread.

notes: Dudu pulls the hat down over her brow with both hands, annoyance marks above
Dumisani reaches out, eyebrows up, worried
illustration.only_in_image: Dudu's embarrassment-anger at failing and Dumisani's worry that he pushed her are carried by faces and posture only.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
He takes Dudu’s hat
from her head,
balls it up, and puts it
in her hand.
“Point your other
hand at the window,”
he says.
“Now throw from
your shoulder.”
Dudu takes a deep
breath and throws.
Her hat swoops up,
opens like a gliding bird,
flies through the window,
and disappears.
pages.action: Dumisani shows her how to throw; her hat glides through the window

notes: Two round vignettes show the coaching step by step: hat balled in her hand, then Dumisani behind her guiding the aim
A burst of lines around the window as the hat flies out
The rhino appears beside the window as if watching
illustration.only_in_image: How the solution physically works: the vignettes show Dumisani standing behind her and placing her arm, aim hand out, ball in the throwing hand. The step-by-step layout slows the moment.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Yes!”
Dudu and Dumisani shout,
lifting their arms in victory.
pages.action: Both shout and lift their arms in victory
pages.page_turn_note: The next spread is wordless: the turn carries the realisation without a word.

notes: Both children cheer with fists up
The rhino on the shelf raises one arm too
illustration.only_in_image: The stuffed rhino lifts its arm and smiles with them, a toy joining the celebration that the text never mentions.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.action: They freeze, realising both hats are gone
pages.change: Victory flips into the problem: no hats
pages.page_turn_note: A wordless page between the cheer and the shout to the teacher.

notes: Close-up: both stare, mouths open, shock lines above heads
The rhino has small shock lines too
illustration.only_in_image: The whole realisation is picture-only: the text is silent, and the faces say the hats are gone for good. The rhino mirrors their shock.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
“TEACHER!”
Dudu shouts to Teacher Lethabo.
“Our hats
fell out
the window!”
pages.action: Dudu shouts to the teacher that their hats fell out
pages.change: The problem is handed to an adult offstage; the story stops there
pages.question_created: Will they get the hats back, and will they get in trouble?

notes: Both shout with arms raised; the teacher is not drawn
The rhino sits smiling on the shelf behind them
illustration.only_in_image: The teacher never appears and the hats are never fetched; the smiling rhino behind them keeps the tone a joke rather than a scolding. The closing vignette repeats the laughing picture, turning the ending back to fun.

pages.label: INFERRED
